title: Finite-origin evaluation transpose descends to common-stage Hom groups
statement:
theorem internal_hom_universal_of_comparison
    (B : Duality D l hl Ω X)
    (permitted : ∀ K : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X,
      commonStageHomPairs l Ω X (op K, B.omega))
    (_comparison : B.duality.dual ≅ homDual l Ω X B.omega permitted)
    (hproperties : DualityProperties D l hl Ω X B.val) :
    ∀ (K P : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X),
      Function.Bijective (fun h : P ⟶ B.duality.dual.obj (op K) ↦
        (CoefQbarTensor D l hl Ω X).map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 K) h) ≫ B.evaluation K)

proof.text: Choose a common compositum for K and P. For every later stage, use the finite tensor-Hom adjunction and its prescribed duality comparison to prove that the evaluation transpose is bijective. This is the counit formula for the adjunction, conjugated by an isomorphism of its right-hand object.

Use the normalized finite evaluation square, including endpoint isomorphisms, to show that finite evaluation transposes commute with scalar extension. Tensor-inclusion naturality and its coefficient square identify these transposes with the stated global evaluation map. The recorded dual and dualizing-object inclusion squares identify the source and target Hom groups.

Every global morphism has a representative at a sufficiently large common stage, and equality of two included finite morphisms is equality after further scalar extension. For surjectivity, represent the target morphism and apply finite-stage surjectivity. For injectivity, refine representatives to a common stage, refine again until their evaluation images agree, and apply finite-stage injectivity. Compatibility identifies the resulting included maps with the original global maps.

proof_origin.place: H1: finite-adjunction transpose and eventual-equality proof of retained coefficient-transport step 5; normalized tensor and evaluation compatibility proved in six support modules.
